title: Kth Largest
statement:
A leaderboard has scores in `scores` (duplicates allowed, each entry counts). If you sorted them from highest to lowest, the **k-th largest** is the score at position `k` (counting from 1).

Return the k-th largest score.

examples.explanation: Sorted high to low: 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. The 2nd is 5.
Sorted high to low: 6, 5, 5, 4, ... The 4th is 4 (duplicates count).

hints.nudge: You do not need the whole list in order, only the top k scores. Which of those k is the smallest?
hints.pattern: A min-heap that never holds more than k items.
hints.walkthrough: Sorting everything is O(n log n) and works. A min-heap of size k does better when k is small: push each score, and whenever the heap grows beyond k, remove its smallest item. After all scores are processed, the heap contains the k largest, and its smallest element (the top) is exactly the k-th largest. Each push or pop costs O(log k), so O(n log k) overall. Java: PriorityQueue. C++: priority_queue with greater<int>. Python: heapq. JavaScript has no built-in heap, so write a small one or sort.
